operation.body:
## Goal
Implement the adopted D-020 CPU tick and thermal-category normalization contracts behind injected fake readers, without native implementations or live CLI wiring. Deliver one PR for this sampled-source substep.

## Acceptance criteria
- Add a fixed CPU-tick reader contract for four Intel natural_t counters (user, system, idle, nice), with an explicit returned element count and typed failure. Accept exactly four UInt32 counters and widen each to the existing UInt64 CPU tick representation. Zero and UInt32.max are valid counters; malformed counts/storage yield a fixed invalid gap. A generic Mach failure is error, never guessed permission denial.
- Retain fixed source identity public.mach.cpu_ticks.v1 and supplied check time. Expose successful raw counters for future CPUActivityDelta use, not a fabricated activity percentage. Verify synthetic delta use preserves first-sample/zero-total/reset gaps and actual idle zero; do not add runtime baseline management.
- Add a fixed thermal reader contract with nominal/fair/serious/critical and unknown/future state. Known states yield unitless thermal-pressure categories with public.foundation.thermal_state.v1 provenance. Unknown becomes unverified/null with a fixed reason, never a raw numeric value, temperature, safety or throttling claim. Document that nominal can be returned on unsupported systems.
- Each adapter performs one injected read only; invalid empty check metadata fails before any read. No arbitrary selectors/flavors, retry, fallback or source side effect is introduced. Fixture tests cover every category/failure, counter/order/count bounds, null/provenance/JSON behavior, and reader isolation.
- Keep CLI live refusal and existing synthetic behavior. Update development/design status and project architecture pointers with precise limits. Run synthetic product and adapter checks, integrated review, signed PR and CI; require human review/merge for input validation under security policy.

## Constraints
Parent Project #1; current local self-correcting-review with conditional Low-risk auto-merge. Owner adopted D-020 in comment 6897940905, with staged fake-source validation first. Implementing that approved design requires no repeated design approval; validation is High risk under security policy and cannot agent-merge. Preserve private reusable workflow, historical transcription and unrelated .gitlab/.
Risks: counter order/width confusion, zero counters mistaken for idle activity, Mach error guessed as denial, nominal mistaken for safe temperature, fake provenance mistaken for live evidence. Decision queue: no blocking material choice; native count/layout/resource/return-code audit, OS-version and battery adapters, runtime baseline/failure policy, worker/IPC and capture remain separate.

## Out of scope
Native APIs/shims or calls, hardware tests, privilege, workloads, SMC, OS-version/battery adapters, workers/IPC/processes/deadlines, sampling integration, persistence, live CLI/report wiring, dependencies/toolchains/CI changes, GUI/control/recovery, background automation and a second goal.

## Relevant context
D-020: https://github.com/szymoniwacz/mac-thermal-control/issues/1#issuecomment-6897940905; docs/public-telemetry-adapter-review.md adopted at 371055d742b05ecccc0572549c192be6f3f2f4de; docs/discovery-specification.md; docs/development.md; Sources/DiscoveryCore/; .ai/project/ and .ai/docs/project-requirements.md. All delegated goals 2,7,9,11,13,15,17,19,21 terminal via merged PRs 3,8,10,12,14,16,18,20,22. Main 488c0c10435076ddeefb45e35383f487c15b428c and CI 43743670450 green; latest PR-head checks green; no deferred owner checks.
Rollback: reviewed forward revert PR; no report store or installed service.
